items.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023
items.q: the conductor, a wonderful English conductor, Christopher Ward... took it upon himself and conducted

ctx.x: About your expectations of your piece when someone else is conducting it?

That’s right. Yeah this was my first experience. And the conductor, a wonderful English conductor, Christopher Ward, he also conducts the Memphis Orchestra I think, he took it upon himself and conducted — oh man — it was just a wonderful thing to see. So I’m sorry to go on but it’s like yes, somebody believing in music that I believed in. It’s not commercial stuff you know, it’s not high art but it’s my best attempt and to see somebody like on a court going like that or cuing this and it’s all visceral to me…

know, and there it is. And it says it on paper there with my pencil that went into the computer. So that’s a joyous feeling. And the other thing too is the German audiences, they’re a different kind of animal. I mean I was sitting to the side discreetly just observing the symphony playing and a lot of the audience was sitting on the edge of their seats like listening, you know, attentively. It’s like woo! So it’s yeah, that’s a whole experience in music, and that’s why the boy got on the boat I guess is because…
